## Headline
AI stocks trigger Wall Street's worst day since April 2025

## Mood
Risk-off. The VIX jumped roughly 70%, its biggest one-day surge in almost two years. The selling started in chips and spread to the whole market.

## What moved and why
**Post-election AI trade unwinds, S&P 500 tumbles** [Stocks]
Why it happened: Investors reacted to a Democratic midterm sweep with an AI sell-off. They worried about possible Democratic scrutiny of data centre expansion. Hedging by options market makers and volatility-control funds added to the selling.
Why it matters: All 11 S&P 500 sectors closed lower. Forced selling can overshoot, so volatility may stay high.

**Loonie slides after Canada's surprise job losses** [FX]
Why it happened: Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October when analysts expected a gain of 13,600. The unemployment rate rose to 6.7%. Global equity volatility added to the pressure.
Why it matters: Weak jobs data lowered the odds of another Bank of Canada hike. That narrows the rate gap with the US and weakens the Canadian dollar.

**Fed hike bets build even as long yields ease** [Rates]
Why it happened: US payrolls rose 165,000 in October and unemployment dipped to 4.1%. CME FedWatch put the chance of a December quarter-point hike at 76.8%.
Why it matters: The 10-year yield has fallen from a 5.31% peak on Oct. 5 to about 4.86%. Markets are pricing tighter near-term policy while worrying about growth.

## Deals
- **Stock merger, Marvell / Lumentum, $115B enterprise value.** Lumentum holders get 4.5 Marvell shares each. The logic is to combine electrical and optical technologies for AI connectivity. Marvell fell 28.1% on the week.
- **Minority stake purchase, Blackstone-led group / Mitsubishi unit holding an LNG Canada interest, US$3.1B.** CPP Investments, OMERS, IMCO and PSP Investments joined Blackstone to buy 49.9% of the unit. The appeal is long-life export infrastructure with steady returns.
- **Acquisition, AMD / Taalas (Toronto), about US$2.9B.** AMD disclosed the price of the cash-and-stock deal; US$1.4B depends on conditions. The aim is to add AI inference chip talent in Canada.

## What's coming today
- **Sunday:** No major scheduled data. Next week's tone depends on Tuesday's CPI.
- **Monday, 10:00 ET:** Wholesale inventories. A minor read on the economy.
- **Monday, 11:00 ET:** NY Fed consumer expectations survey. It shows how households see inflation.
- **Monday, 1:00 pm ET:** US Treasury sells $58B of 3-year notes. A test of demand for bonds.
- **Monday, after close:** Take-Two and Skydance report.
- **Tuesday, 8:30 ET:** US October CPI. It is the key input for the December Fed decision.

## Canada corner
- The S&P/TSX composite rose 183.82 points on Friday. The week was volatile.
- The Bank of Canada's rate hike last week was its first since July 2023. Weak jobs data now clouds the next move.
- The Bank and the finance ministry renewed the 2% inflation target in a five-year framework.
- Canadian Natural will buy back $800M of shares a month in November and December.

## The takeaway
- **IB & Markets:** If someone asks you about markets today: it was a positioning-driven AI de-risking, not a credit event. The next test is whether CPI backs the Fed's December hike.
- **Consulting:** A data-centre supplier should stress-test demand and permitting scenarios under tougher regulation. It should also avoid depending on a few hyperscaler customers.
- **Accounting:** Marvell's fixed exchange ratio means the purchase price is measured at the closing share price. A lower stock price shrinks goodwill, and auditors will test the fair value of the acquired assets.
